# Page 16^page=16
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS PM Narendra Modi Launches 246 Tribal Development Projects Worth Rs 3,000 Crore on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas 2026 In November 2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 246 development projects worth approximately Rs 3,000 crore during the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas 2026 programme held in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, through video conferencing.  The programme was organised to mark the 151st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. Exam Hints:  What? Inauguration and foundation stone laying of 246 tribal development projects  Inaugurated by: PM Narendra Modi  Where? Gadchiroli, Maharashtra (via video conferencing)  Occasion: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas 2026  Projects Inaugurated: 173  Foundation Stones Laid: 73  Focus Areas: education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities  Major Projects: 38 EMRS, 100 Multipurpose Centres, 19 new EMRS and 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres Key Highlights of the Development Projects: Aim: The projects aim to strengthen education, healthcare, livelihoods, tribal heritage preservation and community infrastructure across India. Inauguration of 173 Projects: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): PM Modi inaugurated 38 EMRS to expand access to quality residential education for tribal students. Multipurpose Centres: He inaugurated 100 Multipurpose Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) to support public service delivery and community activities in tribal areas. Other Projects: Additional projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) were inaugurated to improve essential services and infrastructure. Tribal Heritage and Research Institutions: Tribal Research Institute (TRI): PM Modi inaugurated the new TRI building at Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, to support tribal research, documentation and preservation of indigenous traditions. Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum: He inaugurated the museum at Aizawl, Mizoram, dedicated to preserving Mizo tribal history, culture and freedom struggles.  The museum is named after Ropuiliani, a 19th-century Mizo chieftainess who resisted British colonial rule. Foundation Stones for 73 Projects: New EMRS: Foundation stones were laid for 19 new schools to strengthen educational facilities for tribal children. Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs): PM Modi laid the foundation stones for 12 TMMCs to improve market access and livelihood opportunities for tribal producers. Other Development Works: Foundation stones were laid for 42 additional projects under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 17 Daily Content PDF About Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas: Observance: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas is celebrated annually on 15 November to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda and honour the contributions of tribal freedom fighters. Government Recognition: The Government of India declared the observance in 2021 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations. About Birsa Munda: Bhagwan Birsa Munda was a prominent tribal freedom fighter from present-day Jharkhand who led the Ulgulan (Great Tumult) movement against British colonial rule and exploitative practices affecting tribal communities. 2026 Observance: Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada was observed nationwide from 1 to 15 November 2026, culminating in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. About Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA): Union Minister- Jual Oram (Constituency- Sundargarh, Odisha) Minister of State (MoS)- Durgadas Uikey (Constituency- Betul, Madhya Pradesh, MP) India–Belarus Hold 12th Inter-Governmental Commission Meeting in New Delhi; Sign Scientific Cooperation Programme On 16 November 2026, India and Belarus held the 12th Session of India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission (IGC) on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation in New Delhi, Delhi.  The meeting was co-chaired by Union Minister of State (MoS) Jitin Prasada, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) and H.E. Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Belarus. Exam Hints:  What? 12th India–Belarus IGC meeting  Co-Chairs: Union MoS Jitin Prasada,MoCI; Maxim Ryzhenkov, Foreign Minister of Belarus  Key Outcome: Protocol of the 12th Session signed; Roadmap for Cooperation (2027–2031) discussed.  Scientific Agreement: 2nd PoC (2027–2029) between CSIR & NASB About the 12th IGC Meeting: Objective: Both sides reviewed bilateral relations and explored opportunities to expand trade, investment, industrial cooperation and scientific partnerships. Framework: Both countries discussed the Roadmap for Cooperation for 2027–2031 to identify future priorities and guide bilateral economic engagement, with the 13th India–Belarus IGC session scheduled to be held in 2027. Protocol: The two Co-Chairs signed the Protocol of the 12th IGC Session, reaffirming both countries’ commitment to strengthening cooperation in trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural sectors.  Both countries explored cooperation across manufacturing, banking, agriculture, healthcare, tourism, education, science and technology, construction and customs India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum: Held alongside the IGC session, the forum brought together business representatives, industry associations and government institutions from both countries, with Belarusian companies representing sectors such as machinery, mining equipment, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, microelectronics, agriculture, engineering, water treatment and food processing. CSIR–NASB Sign Second Programme of Cooperation: Overview: On the sidelines of the Commission meeting, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) signed the Second Programme of Cooperation (PoC) (2027–2029) to promote joint scientific research.

# Page 18^page=18

Kalaiselvi, Director General (DG), CSIR and Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), and Dr. A.V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman, Presidium of NASB in New Delhi. Research Collaboration: The agreement provides a renewed framework for collaborative research projects, scientific exchanges and innovation-driven partnerships in mutually identified areas of science and technology. Background: The Second PoC builds on the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Scientific and Technical Cooperation signed between CSIR and NASB on 22 May 2023.  CSIR and NASB proposed launching the Second Joint Call for RDI Proposals on 27 November 2026 to support new collaborative research projects between Indian and Belarusian scientists. About Belarus: Belarus, formerly known as Belorussia or White Russia, was the smallest of the three Slavic republics in the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) and declared independence from the USSR in 1991. President – Alexander Lukashenko Capital – Minsk Currency – Belarusian ruble (BYN) Ministry of Culture Launches AI-Powered Semantic Search Platform ‘Sanskriti’ for Indian Heritage In November 2026, Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture launched ‘Sanskriti’, an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered conversational assistant, as part of its semantic search and knowledge discovery platform on its official website, culture.gov.in, to provide unified access to authentic information on India’s cultural heritage. Exam Hints:  What? Launch of ‘Sanskriti’ AI-powered search platform  Launched by: Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, MoC  Platform: Ministry of Culture website  Digital Coverage: Approximately 65 heritage portals  Language Support: 22 Indian languages through BHASHINI  Technology: AI, Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). About ‘Sanskriti’ AI-powered search platform: Integration: The platform integrates information from approximately 65 digital portals of the Ministry and its institutions, with multilingual access in 22 Indian languages through the government’s BHASHINI(BHASHa INterface for India) platform. Search Capabilities: Using Natural Language Processing (NLP), embeddings, knowledge graphs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the platform understands everyday-language queries and provides contextually relevant answers with source citations. Authentic Information: Uses open-source, on-premises, Large Language Model (LLM)-agnostic architecture to retrieve information exclusively from official Ministry portals, providing cited answers without relying on open-internet content and allowing users to flag errors. Digital Collections: The platform provides live access to major databases, including Gyan Bharatam, Abhilekh Patal, Indian Culture and Mera Gaon Meri Dharohar.

Expedition Team: A total of 24 cyclists, comprising 14 Indian and 10 Sri Lankan NCC personnel. India Post Releases Commemorative Stamp Honouring Biogas Pioneer Ram Bux Singh In November 2026, the Department of Posts (DoP), under the Ministry of Communications, released a commemorative postage stamp of Rs 5 denomination to honor Ram Bux Singh (1925–2016), an Indian scientist and internationally recognised pioneer in biogas technology and Renewable energy(RE).  The postage stamp was jointly released by Union Minister of State (MoS) Ramdas Athawale, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJ&E), and Col. Akhilesh Kumar Pandey, Chief Postmaster General, Delhi Circle, at the Minister’s residence in New Delhi (Delhi). Exam Hints:  What? Release of commemorative postage stamp  Honouring: Ram Bux Singh  Released By: Department of Posts, MoC  Denomination: Rs 5  Other Key Release: Book titled “Complete Guide to Biogas-Renewable Energy from Waste: Featuring the Legacy of Dr. Ram Bux Singh” About Ram Bux Singh: Pioneer in Biogas Technology: Known as the “Father of Modern Biogas”, he inaugurated one of India’s earliest successful gobar gas plants at Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh (UP), in 1957.  Gobar Gas Research Station: He served as Officer-in-Charge for 16 years at Asia’s first Gobar Gas Research Station in Ajitmal, UP, advancing biogas technology.

MoC&I Clarifies DPIIT and DoC as Competent Authorities for Issuing Defence Manufacturing Licences In November 2026, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) clarified that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Department of Commerce (DoC) are the competent authorities to issue industrial licences for defence manufacturing under the Industries (Development and Regulation) (IDR) Act, 1951.  DPIIT issues licences for manufacturing units outside Special Economic Zones (SEZs), while the DoC licenses units within SEZs and Export Oriented Units (EOUs). Exam Hints:  What? DPIIT and DoC authorised to issue industrial licences for defence purposes  By Whom? MoC&I  Legal Framework: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.  Responsibility: DPIIT – Defence manufacturers located outside SEZs; DoC – Manufacturers located within SEZs and EOUs  Application Portal: National Single Window System (NSWS). About Defence Industrial Licensing Authorisation: Legal Framework: Section 11 of the IDR Act, 1951, mandates licensing for scheduled industries, with DPIIT covering four categories: defence equipment, industrial explosives, specified hazardous chemicals, and tobacco products. Application: Industrial licence applications under the IDR Act, 1951, and Arms Act, 1959, are submitted through the National Single Window System (NSWS) and circulated by DPIIT to relevant ministries, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and State Governments for comments.  IDR Act licences are valid for 15 years, extendable by 3 years, while Arms Act licences remain valid for the company’s lifetime if the facility is established within 7 years. Approval: The Minister in charge of DPIIT (Union Minister Piyush Goyal) approves or rejects licences based on the Licensing Committee’s recommendations, while SEZ units follow the separate approval framework under the SEZ Act, 2005. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS India Re-elected to International Telecommunication Union Council for 2027–2030 Term On 16 November 2026, India was re-elected to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for the 2027–2030 term during the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26), scheduled from 9 to 27 November 2026 at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Center in Doha, Qatar.  India secured 151 votes, receiving the 3rd-highest votes among 15 contesting countries in Region E (Asia and Australasia), after Qatar (1st – 165 votes) and Saudi Arabia (2nd – 155 votes).

India re-elected to ITU Council  Term: 2027–2030 (4 years)  During: 22nd ITU Plenipotentiary Conference, Doha, Qatar  Regional Rank: 3rd-highest votes in Region E (Asia and Australasia), which has 13 seats  Other Election:  ITU Secretary-General: Doreen Bogdan-Martin (USA)  Deputy Secretary-General – Adel Darwish (Bahrain). India’s Role and Significance: Global Representation: India’s re-election strengthens its role in international telecommunications governance and digital connectivity initiatives. Responsible Ministry: Ministry of Communications through the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), which serves as India’s nodal department for engagement with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). About ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026: Frequency: The Plenipotentiary Conference is ITU’s highest policy-making body, convened once every four years to determine the organisation’s strategic direction, policies and leadership. Key Elections: On 12 November 2026, Doreen Bogdan-Martin of the United States of America(USA) was re-elected as ITU Secretary-General, securing 164 votes out of 173 votes cast.  Adel Darwish (Bahrain) was elected as the Deputy Secretary-General . About ITU: Overview: The ITU was established on 17 May 1865 in Paris, France, as the International Telegraph Union and renamed in 1934. It became a specialised agency of the United Nations (UN) under a 1947 agreement and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. ITU Council: It serves as the organisation’s governing body between Plenipotentiary Conferences, overseeing its activities, policies and strategies, managing working groups and preparing draft strategic and financial plans. Election: The Council comprises 48 Member States, elected every four years from five geographical regions. Regional Allocation: Region A (Americas) – 9 seats; Region B (Western Europe) – 8 seats; Region C (Eastern Europe and Northern Asia) – 5 seats; Region D (Africa) – 13 seats; Region E (Asia and Australasia) – 13 seats. About Ministry of Communications: Union Minister – Jyotiraditya Madhavrao Scindia (Constituency – Guna, Madhya Pradesh, MP). Overview of Union Minister Piyush Goyal Visit to Egypt from November 15 to 16, 2026 Union Minister Piyush Goyal, Ministry of Commerce & Industry (MoCI) undertook a two-day visit to Egypt from November 15 to 16, 2026, marking his first bilateral visit to an African country.  He was accompanied by a delegation of over 130 business leaders and startups to strengthen bilateral trade, investment, industrial cooperation and business partnerships.

Exam Hints:  What? Union Minister Piyush Goyal, MoCI visited Egypt  Aim: To Expand bilateral trade, investment and industrial cooperation between the two nations.  Key Business Engagements: 7th Session of the India–Egypt JTC, 6th India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) Meeting and Business Forum, and the India–Egypt Startups Forum  Key Outcomes: Bilateral Trade Target (USD 12 billion within 5 years); Setting up a JWG to explore ToR for PTA or FTA; India to host 8th India-Egypt JTC in New Delhi (2028). Key Highlights of Visit: 7th India–Egypt JTC: The Union Minister Piyush Goyal, along with his Egyptian counterpart Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, co-chaired the 7th session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) held in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital (Cairo), marking its first ministerial-level session to strengthen bilateral economic cooperation. Key Proposals by India: During the event, Union Minister Piyush Goyal announced that the central banks of India and Egypt are working to promote bilateral trade in their respective local currencies. In addition, India also proposed to link its Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with Egypt’s digital payment system.  Bilateral Trade Target: Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, from existing USD 6.5 billion in the Financial Year 2025-26(FY26) to USD 12 billion within 5 years.  Key Outcomes: Both countries agreed to set up a Joint Working Group (JWG) to explore the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) or Free Trade Agreement (FTA) to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, enhance access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries. Also, both Ministers signed the Agreed Minutes of the 7th India–Egypt JTC.  8th India-Egypt JTC: India will host the 8th India-Egypt JTC in New Delhi in 2028, or earlier, on a mutually convenient date. 6th India-Egypt JBC: During the visit, Union Minister Piyush Goyal, alongside Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, participated in the 6th India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC).  Areas of Discussions: The discussions were mainly focused on sectors such as: chemicals and petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, food processing and agri-business, Renewable Energy (RE) and green hydrogen, among others. India-Egypt Business Forum: The Union Minister Goyal also attended the India-Egypt Business Forum, which brought together over 300 companies from both countries to explore trade and investment opportunities under their Strategic Partnership (SP).  While addressing the session, he proposed a 4-point action agenda ahead of the 80th anniversary of diplomatic relations between India and Egypt in 2027. India-Egypt Startups Forum: As part of his key business engagements, Union Minister Piyush Goyal alongside Egypt’s Minister of Planning and Economic Development Dr. Ahmed Rostom participated in the India–Egypt Startups Forum, which brought together startups, incubators, accelerators, venture investors and representatives of relevant government agencies from both countries.  The Forum provided a platform for around 50 Indian and Egyptian startups to present their respective innovation ecosystems, share experiences and explore collaboration across identified sectors.
